title: The source of emulation
hook: Twelver Shia follow a living senior jurist, a marja', in matters of law

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ja'far al-Sadiq's school, and your line: the school of the sixth imam. Which small trust did you keep exactly? Day one thousand one hundred ninety-nine.

On a shelf in a Shia home there may be a thick paperback of numbered rulings. Prayer. Fasting. Buying and selling. Travel. What to do if you lose count in the middle of a prayer. The author's name is on the cover, and he's alive. In the house next door, the shelf may hold the same kind of book by a different author. Each adult in the family may have chosen their own. Yesterday was the school; today, the living person a believer follows inside it, and why that person has to be living.
screen: `A PAPERBACK OF NUMBERED RULINGS.` → `A LIVING NAME ON THE COVER.` → `CHOSEN BY EACH ADULT.`

segments.voice: The word is marja': a reference, a place you turn to. In full, marja' al-taqlid, the source of emulation. Taqlid means following someone else's ruling. Ja'fari books of practical rulings open with a choice. In matters of law, an adult can take one of three roads. Become a mujtahid, a jurist able to derive rulings from the sources. Or act with precaution, doing what satisfies every serious opinion, which takes a good deal of knowledge too. Or follow a mujtahid. The third is the road these books expect someone without that training to take. The one followed is the marja'. The books list what he must be: adult, sane, just, a Twelver Shia, and a mujtahid. And they add: as best you can tell, follow the most learned, by asking people of knowledge you trust. Then the condition in today's line. Living. In these books, you may not begin following a scholar who has already died. The reason Shia jurists give is that the law keeps meeting new questions, new medicines, new machines, new kinds of money, and a living jurist can answer them. The door of reasoning stays open. Whether you may stay with a marja' who died while you were following him is something they answer differently, and, fittingly, that's a question you put to your living marja'. This following has limits. It covers practical law: how to pray, fast, trade. The books ask each person to reach the foundations of belief for themselves. And Shia jurists explain taqlid with a familiar picture: the one who doesn't know turns to the one who does, the way a patient turns to a doctor.
screen: `MARJA': A SOURCE TO TURN TO.` · `THREE ROADS: REASON, CAUTION, FOLLOW.` · `LEARNED, JUST, AND LIVING.` · `A PATIENT AND A DOCTOR.`

segments.voice: The practice: learn what a marja' is. Say the three roads to yourself, slowly: derive it, be cautious, or follow someone who can. Then think of one part of your own life where you lean on someone who knows more than you. A doctor. A mechanic. An aunt who knows the family recipes. How did you choose them? What would make you stop trusting them? Hold that person in mind for a few breaths, with some gratitude. If you pray, you can ask for good guides. The bell holds the time.
Marja'. A source to turn to: in Twelver Shia law, the living senior jurist whose practical rulings a believer follows. Today's word.
Your line: follow the living scholar. Today, ask one real question of someone who knows more than you, and take the answer seriously. Day one thousand one hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: Twelver Shia Muslims choose a living marja' whose practical rulings they follow, consulting his book of rulings, his website or his offices with questions about prayer, fasting, trade and daily life.

fork.setup: you're a young Shia adult choosing whose rulings to follow. your grandfather followed a great marja' who has since died. what do the books of rulings tell you?
options: begin following the late marja', as your grandfather did.
choose a living marja', the most learned you can identify.
work out every ruling yourself, with no training.
fork.reveal: a living marja', the most learned you can identify by asking trusted people. the law meets new questions, and a living jurist can answer them.

what it means: a living senior jurist whose practical rulings each believer chooses to follow.

sources.ref: Risalah 'amaliyyah (books of practical rulings by Twelver maraji'), opening rulings on taqlid, ihtiyat and ijtihad

notes: The three roads (ijtihad, ihtiyat, taqlid) are stated from the opening rulings of standard risalahs; confirm.

Conditions of the marja' (adult, sane, just, Twelver, mujtahid; living; most learned where identifiable): confirm the list and wording; some maraji' list further conditions (e.g., male, born legitimately) not mentioned here.
'You may not begin following a deceased mujtahid' (ibtida'an), with remaining (baqa') answered differently: confirm framing.
Taqlid limited to practical law; foundations of belief (usul al-din) reached by each person: confirm.
The patient-and-doctor picture for ruju' al-jahil ila al-'alim: confirm it is a usual explanation.
